37.0.0.en: 1 The hand of the LORD was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the LORD, and set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones, 2 And caused me to pass by them round about: and, behold, there were very many in the open valley; and, lo, they were very dry. 3 And he said unto me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And I answered, "O Lord GOD, thou knowest." 4 Again he said unto me, "Prophesy upon these bones, and say unto them, O ye dry bones, hear the word of the LORD. 5 Thus saith the Lord GOD unto these bones; Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live: 6 And I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and ye shall live; and ye shall know that I am the LORD."

37.0.1.en: When the people were driven out of their homeland because of their idolatrous abominations and their shedding of blood, their cities were turned into ruins in which no one dwelt, and they became like a valley full of bones, many and very dry. They became like a battlefield on which all the men were slain and no one was found to bury them, so they became many scattered bones, which the sun had scorched and the winds had blown upon for a long time until they were very dry. In other words, they became like an open grave holding lifeless bones! This is not a picture of the cities, but rather a picture of the people themselves, who were scattered in many places with a broken soul, and so became like a valley of death containing dry bones, in need of One who would raise them from their death, gather them together again and grant them life.

37.0.2.en: In truth, this vision presented to us the resurrection from the dead as a divine work that continues throughout history, from many aspects, among them:

37.0.3.en: a. The resurrection of the ancient people by their return from the Babylonian captivity once again to the Promised Land, as one kingdom with one new heart...

37.0.4.en: b. The resurrection of souls from the death of sin to enter into the life of righteousness and holiness, the heavenly, spiritual, divine life, by the action of the Word of God incarnate, the Giver of life.

37.0.5.en: c. The resurrection of the Church of the New Testament from all the Gentiles and peoples, those who received the faith and were granted resurrection from death to life, to live as a heavenly bride, through the preaching of the Gospel.

37.0.6.en: d. The resurrection of the bodies of the saints on the great day of the Lord, when the souls that had already enjoyed the resurrection through their faith in the Lord Christ receive the bodies that belong to them, so that man may remain soul and body in eternal glories. The expressions of this chapter were used in the early Church as a testimony to the resurrection. We may mention, for example, the scholar Tertullian, who agreed that this prophecy refers to the resurrection of the people from death (the captivity), and at the same time saw in it a declaration of the reality of the body, which cannot be denied. St. Ambrose also says: [How great is the compassionate love of the Lord! He took the prophet as a witness of the resurrection to come, so that we might see it through his eye. For not everyone could be taken as an eyewitness, but in this one man we have become witnesses.]

37.0.7.en: e. Some see that this chapter prophesies about the rising of Israel and its acceptance of faith in the Lord Christ at the end of the ages, when the Holy Spirit will work in them and raise them from the death of unbelief.

37.0.8.en: As for the vision, its description expresses precisely the work of God in raising us from the dead. The vision begins with his words: "The hand of the LORD was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the LORD, and set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones, and caused me to pass by them round about: and, behold, there were very many in the open valley; and, lo, they were very dry" [1-2]. If the hand of the Lord, as we have already seen, signifies the Second Hypostasis, the incarnate Son of God, then it was not possible for the prophet Ezekiel to go down to the valley, nor to see the many scattered dry bones, nor to behold the resurrection, unless the Lord Christ took hold of him by His hand, led him by His Spirit and brought him down to the valley.

37.0.9.en: It is the work of the Lord Christ, the hand of the Lord, to bring us out of ourselves by the Spirit of the Lord and to go first with us to the valley, so that we go down there and see the death in which we are, and then He returns and raises us to the joy of the resurrection with Him. It is a promise to send His Holy Spirit to reprove of sin (Jn 16:8), this divine Spirit who opens our insight, so that we recognize our death, and then we receive the resurrection within us.

37.0.10.en: In other words, if our inner Ezekiel wished to go down to the valley by himself, he could not come out of the "I", for it is the work of the Spirit of the Lord to bring him out so that he may see through the lens of the Lord and not through the dark human lens. And if he went down and discovered death, he would be utterly shattered, for he could not touch the resurrection and experience it except through the Lord Christ Himself, who rose from the dead. For this reason the holy Fathers distinguish between true repentance and human remorse: the first is the fruit of the divine Spirit, who fills the soul with comfort and hope in the moments of repentance and amid the tears, while human remorse drives to despair, as happened with Judas when his conscience reproved him, without his turning to the Savior and asking for the work of the Spirit of the Lord in him.

37.1.s.en: 2. The return of life to the bones:

37.1.0.en: 7 So I prophesied as I was commanded: and as I prophesied, there was a noise, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to his bone. 8 And when I beheld, lo, the sinews and the flesh came up upon them, and the skin covered them above: but there was no breath in them. 9 Then said he unto me, "Prophesy unto the wind, prophesy, son of man, and say to the wind, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live." 10 So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.

37.1.1.en: When the prophet Ezekiel prophesied as the Lord commanded him, there was a noise and a shaking, and then the bones came together, bone to his bone [7]. Perhaps the noise signifies the "Word of God" or the divine voice that gives life and resurrection, while the shaking signifies the intervention of the Spirit of God. As for the bones coming together, bone to his bone, it takes place by an exact divine plan, and in it is an indication of the gathering of the Jewish people from the dispersion and the joining together of the members of each tribe. It also contains a declaration of the completion of the Body of Christ, which is the Church, gathered from every race, tongue and nation, as if they were scattered, dry bones, which the Holy Spirit joined together to become the one holy Body of Christ, working together. In this work there is also a living picture of the work of the Holy Spirit in the human soul that has become a wreck: He joins the bones together in a transcendent way, so that the powers and gifts of man work together in harmony according to a divine plan.

37.2.0.en: "Thus saith the Lord GOD; Come... O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live" [9]. It is the work of God, who sends His Holy Spirit upon the soul that has become like one slain, and gives it life. Here the work of the Spirit does not stop at that, but makes it bear the power of work and service, for He makes of it "an exceeding great army" [10]. It is as though man in his death is a collection of many, very dry bones, and in his resurrection by God he becomes an exceeding great army. In our spiritual life there are no half measures: either a deadly death or a strong and effective life. In the psalm of repentance, when the psalmist met God his Savior, he was not content with his repentance and his return to life after death, but said, "Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee" (Ps 51:13)... He tasted life after death, so he does not cease to preach this life to every transgressor and hypocrite, so that all may enter with him into this new life.

37.3.0.en: 11 Then he said unto me, "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts. 12 Therefore prophesy and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel. 13 And ye shall know that I am the LORD, when I have opened your graves, O my people, and brought you up out of your graves, 14 And shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live, and I shall place you in your own land: then shall ye know that I the LORD have spoken it, and performed it, saith the LORD."

37.4.0.en: Lest the hearer think that what the prophet Ezekiel saw concerns merely the return of the people from captivity to the Promised Land, the Lord made clear that this vision also proclaims the resurrection of the soul that died by withdrawing from its God, and the resurrection of the heart that despair had shattered, so that it became a grave holding dry bones. For this reason the Lord says: "Behold, they say, Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts... Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves" [12]. He speaks with people who are alive according to the body and dead according to the spirit; therefore He opens their inner graves and raises their souls. Here He repeats the expression "O my people"... For after He had called them "the people," they have now, by the power of the resurrection, become "the people of God," and the Lord rejoices to claim them as His own.

37.5.0.en: 15 The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying, 16 "Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions: 17 And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand. 18 And when the children of thy people shall speak unto thee, saying, Wilt thou not shew us what thou meanest by these? 19 Say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his fellows, and will put them with him, even with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand. 20 And the sticks whereon thou writest shall be in thine hand before their eyes. 21 And say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land: 22 And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all: 23 Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things, nor with any of their transgressions: but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God. 24 And David my servant shall be king over them; and they all shall have one shepherd: they shall also walk in my judgments, and observe my statutes, and do them. 25 And they shall dwell in the land that I have given unto Jacob my servant, wherein your fathers have dwelt; and they shall dwell therein, even they, and their children, and their children's children for ever: and my servant David shall be their prince for ever. 26 Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore. 27 My tabernacle also shall be with them: yea, I will be their God, and they shall be my people. 28 And the heathen shall know that I the LORD do sanctify Israel, when my sanctuary shall be in the midst of them for evermore."

37.5.1.en: The Lord asked the prophet Ezekiel to take a stick and write on it "For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions," and another on which to write "For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions," and to join them together as one stick in his hand. It is as though in this symbolic act there is a prophecy of the union of Judah with Ephraim, that is, the southern kingdom with the northern... In this symbol, and in the interpretation that the Lord Himself gave at length, the following is to be noted:

37.5.2.en: a. Resurrection is not an individual work. Although it is a personal work that each person tastes and enjoys personally, he receives the resurrection as an entrance into membership in the one people, the one Church, the bride of the one Christ. When the Apostle Paul spoke to the Ephesians about the Church as the Body of Christ that enjoys the resurrection with Him, he spoke of it not as members isolated from one another, but as members one of another, enjoying the possibilities of the Lord Christ for her. He says about the Church: "That he might gather together in one all things in Christ" (Eph 1:10), "Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all" (Eph 1:23). "In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord: In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit" (Eph 2:21-22). So in Christ I am gathered with all my brethren in the unity of the Spirit, so that the Body may be declared complete, and in Him I grow not alone but as an inseparable part of the one holy temple, and I represent a living portion in the one dwelling of God, that is, in His sanctuaries. My resurrection is an inseparable part of the resurrection of the universal Church, and the resurrection of the whole body is the mystery of my resurrection in the Lord.

37.5.3.en: b. In the parable the Lord chose two sticks that became one stick in the hand of the prophet, as though they were the two beams of the Cross, the vertical beam and the horizontal beam, which came together in the hand of the Lord and so declared unity through the Cross. I have previously presented the sayings of the Fathers about the work of the Cross and its effectiveness in joining us in a vertical unity and a horizontal one. Our first unity is with God, the unity of heaven with earth, while the horizontal unity is the unity of the Gentiles and peoples, or the unity of mankind together through the Cross, for the Apostle says, "But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ... That he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby" (Eph 2:13-16). By the Cross He slew the enmity between heaven and earth, and slew the enmity that was between men and one another.

37.5.4.en: c. The names of all the tribes of the two kingdoms were engraved on the Cross (the two sticks), so that every person might find a place in the bosom of the Crucified One, who is full of love without discrimination.

37.6.0.en: d. The mystery of this one nation, or one people, which enjoyed the resurrection from the dead, is the raising up of "one king [who] shall be king to them all" [22], declaring thus: "David my servant shall be king over them; and they all shall have one shepherd" [24].

37.6.1.en: The mystery of unity is that we all enter "in Christ Jesus," our one Shepherd, and are found in the Beloved (Eph 1:6), and are gathered together: those in heaven and those on earth (Eph 1:10). In Him we enjoy the new creation (Eph 2:10), and He joins us, who were strangers and far off, and made us near to Him (Eph 2:7), that our building may be completed in Him as a living divine sanctuary and the eternal temple of God.

37.7.0.en: e. He raises us up as one Church enjoying the risen life, that is, His divine life, through the everlasting covenant that He made with us, an eternal covenant, in which He pledges not only our resurrection but also our continual growth through His dwelling in our midst and above us... that is, He dwells in the midst of His people, and His people become a divine throne, like the Cherubim, bearing Him above them. This is what He meant by saying, "I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore. My tabernacle also shall be with them" [26-27]. He has placed this covenant in our hands, so that it has become ours and we hold fast to it; through it we are sanctified by His dwelling in us and His receiving us as a throne for Himself... This is the mystery of our sanctification, for He says: "And the heathen shall know that I the LORD do sanctify Israel" [28]. This is the new Israel whom God received as the mystery of His sanctification!

37.7.2.en: * What do You see in me, O my Savior?

37.7.3.en: I am the valley of dry bones!

37.7.4.en: By Your Holy Spirit You grant me the risen life!

37.7.5.en: Instead of death You grant me life!

37.7.6.en: Instead of corruption You grant me purity and holiness!

37.7.7.en: Wonderful is Your work, O You who rose from the dead: You raise me and make of me an exceeding great army!

37.7.8.en: * By Your Holy Spirit You sanctify my emotions and feelings, You sanctify my heart and mind, You sanctify my gifts and capabilities, You sanctify my thoughts, my words and my deeds...

37.7.9.en: And from all this You raise up an exceeding great army!

37.7.10.en: * You raise me, and I unite with the rest of my brethren!

37.7.11.en: You make us one stick, with one heart and one spirit!

37.7.12.en: You are our resurrection and the mystery of our unity!

37.7.13.en: Reign, O Head who rose from the dead, and make us one Church enjoying the risen life!
